metaDescription: Compare Caveday's guided Caves with MySession rooms.
h1: MySession vs Caveday: a flexible alternative to guided Caves
heroDescription: Caveday runs guided Caves on Zoom with a human guide. MySession offers group rooms you can join at any point, scheduled sessions, and 1:1 matching, with tasks and stages inside the room.

sections.heading: The short answer
body: Caveday is built around Caves: guided online focus sessions of 30 minutes, one hour, or three hours, led by a human guide on Zoom, with live Caves scheduled for 20+ hours a day. Members also get a 24/7 Focus Lounge, workshops, and accountability groups. The Starter Pass costs $105 for three months after a 14-day free trial.

MySession is a Caveday alternative for people who want group focus with more flexible entry and the plan on screen. Always-open rooms can be joined at any point in their cycle, scheduled group sessions add a fixed start, and the 1:1 queue covers days when you want one partner. The Free plan covers your first 15 sessions; Pro is $10 a month or $96 a year.
bullets: Join an always-open room at any time
Tasks, intentions, and stages in the room

sections.heading: When a guided Cave is the better fit
body: Choose a Cave if you want a guide to set expectations, run the sprints and breaks, and bring the group back together. A small-group check-in at the start makes your goal concrete, and the shared ending gives you a moment to name a win. That external lead helps on days when deciding how to run the session feels like work in itself.
Caves also suit noisy tasks: everyone is muted, so you can make a call or practise music while others work. Each Cave closes 10 minutes after it starts, so plan to arrive on time.

sections.heading: When MySession may fit better
body: MySession may suit you if you want to start the moment you are ready, including partway through a cycle. Always-open rooms never close and are busiest from about 9 AM to midnight US Eastern time, so you will usually find people working during US daytime and evening hours.

Inside the room, your intention, task list, and the session's stages stay beside the video, and the check-in asks what moved forward. You might write one concrete intention, finish a 30-minute block, mark a task complete, and use the check-in to choose the next step. Nobody needs to be on the same project.
bullets: Visible tasks and intentions inside the room
Optional camera, microphone, chat, and room music

sections.heading: Try the workflow, then decide
body: Use the same small task in both formats. Notice how quickly you got started, whether the structure kept you with the work, and whether the ending left you with a clear next step.

If you consistently need a guide to lead the block, Caveday is worth its price. If you want your task and timer together in a room you can enter at any time, try MySession first; the Free plan makes the test cheap.

The check-in is a chance to say what moved forward, not a test of how much you produced. If the first task took longer than expected, record the next action and choose another block when you are ready.

The browser-based room includes camera, microphone, chat, and optional music controls. Some rooms set their own participation rules, so choose one that fits your environment and privacy needs. You can name an outcome without revealing client documents or personal details.

sections.heading: What happens in a virtual coworking room
body: Virtual coworking is independent work with other people present online. In MySession, participants enter a room from wherever they are, share a small intention, and work on different tasks during the same timed stage. A check-in at the end makes the next step easier to see.

You can keep your task list and the room timeline in view while you work. Chat, camera, microphone, and shared music are available where the room permits them, but the room is designed for doing the work rather than talking through it.

sections.heading: Choose a room for the work you have
body: An always-open room is useful when waiting for a booking would delay the first step. A scheduled group session is useful when the appointment itself helps you commit. Look at the session format and current room rules before joining; a 25-minute block can help you start, while a 50-minute or longer block gives complex work more continuity.

A freelancer can finish a client draft, a student can work through a problem set, and a remote employee can clear an administrative backlog in the same session. Shared presence does not require a shared project.

sections.heading: Coworking or body doubling?
body: The terms overlap. Body doubling describes the focus technique: someone else is present while you do your own task. Virtual coworking describes the online room and group format that makes that presence available. In both cases, the work remains yours.
If you want a simple explanation of the method, start with the body doubling guide. If you want to compare room formats for a remote workday, continue to the remote-worker page.

metaDescription: Compare FLOWN and MySession formats, prices, and rooms.
h1: A FLOWN alternative for structured group focus
heroDescription: FLOWN pairs facilitated sessions with a 24/7 Drop-In and wellbeing extras. MySession focuses on group rooms with tasks and stages built in, plus a free plan and Pro at $10 a month.

sections.heading: The short answer
body: FLOWN is a full focus membership: facilitated sessions of one or two hours, smaller community sessions run by members, a silent 24/7 Drop-In, and recharge sessions such as breathwork and journaling. Membership is $25 a month, $19 a month billed annually, or $900 for lifetime access, after a 30-day free trial. FLOWN Free includes four community sessions a month plus any session on Fridays.

MySession is a FLOWN alternative for people who mainly want the focus room itself: group sessions, always-open rooms, and 1:1 matching, with your intention, tasks, and the session's stages visible in one place. The Free plan covers your first 15 sessions, and Pro is $10 a month or $96 a year.
bullets: Group rooms with tasks and stages built in
Pro at $10/month after the free plan

sections.heading: When FLOWN is the better fit
body: Choose FLOWN if you like professional facilitation and a broader programme around your work. Facilitators lead the focus sessions, and daily planning, guided breaks, and work-with-me videos add structure beyond the focus block itself. FLOWN also sells coaching and accountability groups as add-ons.
FLOWN's Drop-In works like a silent virtual library: you set your own goal and timer and work in the quiet presence of others. That suits people who want company without any conversation.

sections.heading: When MySession is the better fit
body: Choose MySession if the room should carry your plan. You write an intention, keep a task list beside the video, and follow a shared timeline of focus, break, and check-in stages, so nobody has to run their own timer. Always-open rooms are busiest from about 9 AM to midnight US Eastern time; scheduled group sessions add a fixed start when you need one.
Cost and flexibility also matter. Pro is $10 a month, the Free plan includes hosting, and the 1:1 queue covers days when you want a single partner instead of a group.

sections.heading: How to decide
body: Use each free option for the same kind of task for a week: FLOWN's trial or Free plan, and MySession's Free plan. Count the sessions you actually joined, not the ones you planned to join.

If facilitators and wellbeing sessions kept you coming back, FLOWN is worth its price. If you mostly joined when you could drop straight into a room with your task list ready, MySession is the simpler, cheaper fit.

faqItems.question: Is there a free alternative to FLOWN?
faqItems.answer: MySession's Free plan covers your first 15 sessions, including joining and hosting. FLOWN also has a free tier, FLOWN Free, with four community sessions a month and access to any session on Fridays.

faqItems.question: Does MySession have a 24/7 room like FLOWN's Drop-In?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Always-open rooms can be entered at any time. Instead of each person running their own timer, they follow shared focus and break stages and show each person's intention.

faqItems.question: Does MySession have facilitated sessions?
faqItems.answer: Scheduled group sessions are run by community hosts who open the room, invite intentions, and close with a check-in. They are not professional facilitators, so compare the experience if facilitation is your priority.

faqItems.question: Which is cheaper, FLOWN or MySession?
faqItems.answer: As of October 11, 2026, FLOWN is $25 a month or $19 a month billed annually, and MySession Pro is $10 a month or $96 a year. Both have a free option with limits.

faqItems.question: Do I need my camera on in MySession?
faqItems.answer: Most group rooms keep the camera optional unless the host requires it. 1:1 sessions require a camera.

title: 25-Minute Focus Session | MySession
metaDescription: Use a 25-minute focus session to lower start friction, complete a small task, or begin a larger project with a clear stopping point.
heroDescription: A short block is long enough to create progress and small enough to begin when attention or motivation is limited.

sections.heading: Best for a clean start
body: Choose 25 minutes when the primary challenge is beginning. It works well for a bounded task or the first pass of something larger.
bullets: The first step of an avoided task

sections.heading: A simple session plan
body: Spend one minute naming the outcome, protect the work interval from extra planning, and use the closing check-in to decide whether to stop, break, or begin another block.

sections.heading: When to choose longer
body: If setup consumes much of the interval or you are already in flow, a 50- or 90-minute room may protect context better.

faqItems.question: Is 25 minutes a required Pomodoro?
faqItems.answer: No. It is simply a useful short focus length; you can choose the workflow that fits your task.

faqItems.question: Can I do two sessions in a row?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Take a deliberate break and begin another block if it remains useful.

title: 50-Minute Focus Session | MySession
metaDescription: Plan a balanced 50-minute focus session for studying, remote work, writing, and projects that need meaningful progress without a marathon.
heroDescription: A balanced work interval for tasks that need continuity while still benefiting from a nearby break and check-in.

sections.heading: A practical default
body: Fifty minutes leaves room to settle into a task, make visible progress, and close before attention becomes expensive. It is a useful default for everyday knowledge work and study.

sections.heading: Prepare the block
body: Open the required materials before the timer begins, describe one outcome, and put secondary ideas into a note instead of following them during the session.

sections.heading: Close the loop
body: Use the final check-in to record what changed and the exact next action. That reduces the restart cost when you return later.

faqItems.question: Should I take a break after 50 minutes?
faqItems.answer: A short movement or hydration break is usually useful before another sustained block.

faqItems.question: What if my task finishes early?
faqItems.answer: Use the remaining time for a related next action or finish deliberately rather than filling the interval automatically.

title: 90-Minute Focus Session | MySession
metaDescription: Use a structured 90-minute focus session for deep work, long-form writing, complex study, and projects where switching costs are high.
heroDescription: Protect a longer stretch of context for complex work while keeping a visible start, stage structure, and finish.

sections.heading: Best for high-context work
body: Longer sessions are useful when loading the problem takes time: long-form writing, coding, design, research, or difficult academic work.
bullets: Use a planned midpoint break when the timeline includes one

sections.heading: Protect quality, not endurance
body: Ninety minutes should not become a test of sitting still. A short break or change of posture can preserve the quality of the second half without abandoning the shared session.

sections.heading: Avoid using it for every task
body: Small administrative tasks often fit a shorter block. Choose 90 minutes when continuity is genuinely valuable, not because longer automatically means more productive.

faqItems.question: Is a 90-minute session too long for beginners?
faqItems.answer: It can be. Start with 25 or 50 minutes if a shorter commitment makes beginning easier.

faqItems.question: Can the timeline include a break?
faqItems.answer: Yes. MySession session stages can represent work, break, intention, and check-in periods.
